source_issues.note: A100 80+ billion transistor claim and generic CPU ratios need independent correction; avoid reproducing as measured facts.
Amdahl p is baseline-time accelerated fraction, not universally 90–99% ML matrix multiplication; additive formula assumes no overlap.
ResNet/GPT2 p values are constructed assumptions, not hardware benchmarks; bandwidth-bound is not synonym for serial.
TPUv1 ratios conditional benchmark, not a proof general-purpose computing ended; historical8087 100x not needed for scope.
CPU utilization claim generic; training vs inference priorities depend workload/SLO, not universal latency-only inference.
RISC-V fragment incomplete illustrative pseudo-ISA, hardcoded32-byteincrement ignores actualvl and no decrement; avoid importing.
Column-batch Q and K projections then QK^T produce feature-feature not token-token attention. Canonical attention chapter correct.
Fixed16x16 hardware throughput generic notvalid; LayerNorm not one-to-one elementwise because reduction.
Single-cycle sigmoid/tanh/SFU table illustrative notGPU guarantee; preserve distinct scalar/vector/tensor/SFU resources without fabricated latency.
SVE ptrue does not query length; occupancy low does not imply memory-bound; lane divergence details architecture-specific.
Example MMA instruction pseudo-PTX incomplete/invalid signature; canonical real wmma/ptx example preferable.
2:4 hardware requires at most two nonzero entries per group, not exactly. Pattern orientation and metadata matter.
Systolic energy ratio compares uncached naïve DRAM load/store baseline, not CPU/GPU vector unit benchmark.
Output-stationary streamedA/B example must not be described as same path as weight-stationary TPU diagram. Dataflow not universally immutable.
FP32→FP16 does not universally double throughput, precision support depends SKU and instruction.
Mixed hardware/precision lists and prices not apples-to-apples; avoid treating pricing/peak ratios as serving cost measurement.
Illustrative tensor journey incorrectly implies obligatory DMA→L2→L1 path and zero-nanosecond register latency. Existing CUDA hierarchy sections should override.
Irregular address access is not synonymous with memory fragmentation; dense fully connected products are regular.
Generic memory-latency tables are illustrative, not universal device values.
A100 supports FP32 accumulation and FP64 Tensor Core paths; HBM does not universally have lower latency than DDR.
Do not compare aggregate bidirectional NVLink to a one-direction PCIe figure or call a switch's aggregate limit 64 GB/s universally.
The attention score matrix can be quadratic; KV-cache storage grows linearly with sequence length.
Roofline is an upper bound, not an equality guaranteeing achieved throughput.
High arithmetic intensity alone does not establish near-peak performance.
LayerNorm includes a reduction; fusion speedups are not universal constants.
Interactive generation can batch; KV caching does not eliminate weight-bandwidth cost.
Traditional compilers also map operations; NVCC is not directly a high-level model compiler, and Transformer execution is not obligatorily adaptive placement.
Independent factorial configuration counts include illegal dependency orders and coupled decisions; excluded rather than presented as a valid search-space size.
Tokens are not literally unchanged activations through every layer; dataflow is not exclusive to one model family.
NHWC is not a definition of row-major storage. Logical axes and physical strides are distinguished in the new checked example.
Incomplete torch.batch_norm call is not copied as executable code.
Four buffers versus two is not a fourfold memory reduction; training BatchNorm is not pointwise; register spills are not automatically shared-memory allocations.
Source tiling pseudocode omits tail handling and has an invalid split multiplication expression; existing checked examples retain boundary masks.
Transformers are not unconditionally memory-bound.
Keras compile does not universally imply the same JIT contract as torch.compile; arbitrary graph rewrites do not create correct KV caching.
Overlap does not necessarily make a workload compute-bound; JIT exists; runtimes do not automatically retile or fuse arbitrary graphs on every call.
Peak-based GPT-3 timing is hypothetical, not an achievable execution result; observed synchronization percentage is not a fixed baseline serial fraction.
CPU is not always the best NMS target; NPU/DSP power ordering and ML-based runtime scheduling are not universal platform properties.
NPU/CPU carbon example assumes energy and workload values rather than measuring them; use declared energy and carbon boundaries.
CPU utilization alone does not establish faster latency; procurement decisions cannot be based solely on whether one GEMM lies above the ridge.
The absolute claim that accelerators cannot make bytes cheaper to move ignores memory hierarchy, dataflow and packaging design.
